reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently. Ps 34 is a shift+1 psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json: rule=shift, k=1, web_verses 22 / mt_verses 23, mt_title_verses [1]); the row's web:Ps.34.0 = oshb:Ps.34.1 title dual-cite and the WEB.N = MT.N+1 arithmetic on all three quoted verses are correct. All three Hebrew quotes (oshb:Ps.34.2/3/4) collate at byte tier against verse_map_oshb.json (collate.py --json, quotes spliced programmatically from the row text, never hand-typed). The acrostic claim (alef/bet/gimel opening) matches psalm_device_inventory.json's byte-swept first_letters_mt string exactly. The seam at web:Ps.34.3|4 is a genuine tier-1 register shift (plural cohortative 'let's exalt... with me' closing v3 vs singular testimony 'I sought... he answered me' opening v4) and the rejected_alternative names this correctly. Title correctly held as title material (Ps 34 is in the historical-note-title list), not quoted as narrative. No selah/pe-samekh in this psalm (0 of 71 book-wide selah verses fall in Ps 34) so the absence of any disclosure is correct, not a gap.

All three Hebrew quotes (oshb:Ps.34.5/6/7) collate at byte tier. The waw-gap claim is byte-confirmed: psalm_device_inventory.json's acrostics entry for psalm 34 lists letters_missing = waw (ו) and alphabet_letters_in_order skips directly from dalet to he to zayin, matching the row's he/zayin sequence at web:Ps.34.5-6 with no intervening waw verse. Letter assignments (dalet=web.4, he=web.5, zayin=web.6, het=web.7) check out against the byte-swept letter string. The rejected_alternative (treating the gap as textual damage) is correctly dismissed since the surrounding verses are undamaged consecutive text, a defensible literary-critical point. tiling and refs-mirror pass; medium confidence is a reasonable, non-overclaiming calibration for a seam (declarative-generalization to imperative onset) slightly less sharp than the addressee/cohortative shifts flanking it.

Hebrew quotes (oshb:Ps.34.9/10/11) collate at byte tier. Letter sequence tet/yod/kaf (web.8/9/10) matches the byte-swept inventory string continuing past the waw gap. The imperative-cluster driver (taste-and-see, fear-Yahweh, both unaddressed) opening at web.8 and the closing turn to the young-lions wisdom antithesis at web.10 are both accurately described from the text. The rejected_alternative correctly identifies the real rival (folding into the following 'children' address) and gives a specific, checkable reason for rejecting it: no vocative in this span vs. the explicit vocative at web:Ps.34.11. Medium confidence is conservative but not a defect (challenges attach to overclaiming, not underclaiming).

The single Hebrew quote (oshb:Ps.34.12) collates at byte tier. Letters lamed/mem/nun/samekh (web.11-14) match the inventory's byte-swept sequence exactly, including correct use of the samekh glyph. The vocative 'children' (banim) at web:Ps.34.11 is verifiably the psalm's only verse-opening address to a human party (checked against the full WEB text of both psalms), making this the strongest single seam-driver in the cluster; high confidence is well earned. The closing seam (imperative address ending, third-person resuming at web.15) is clean and correctly argued in the rejected_alternative.

Both Hebrew quotes (oshb:Ps.34.16, oshb:Ps.34.23) collate at byte tier. The extra-alphabetic closing pe (web.22 = MT 34:23) is confirmed: the inventory's first_letters_mt string ends ...shin-tav-pe (23 letters against a 22-letter alphabet), and the row correctly does NOT apply unit_type=coda to this verse — that vocabulary term is reserved for the book's doxology/colophon closes (41/72/89/106), not an acrostic's trailing extra letter, so 'strophe' is the correct controlled-vocabulary choice. The cross-reference to the waw gap at web:Ps.34.5-6 in device_notes is verse-anchored (register-compliant) and correctly pulled into boundary_evidence_refs. I tested whether an internal seam (e.g. at web.19|20, the 'many afflictions' turn) would out-warrant the whole-span reading; no addressee/imperative/refrain driver breaks the third-person Yahweh-and-the-righteous discourse across web.15-22, so the 8-verse span (at the top of the ~4-8vv strophe norm) is the best-supported unit; medium confidence appropriately reflects the absence of a finer-grained tier-1 driver inside it.

Ps 35 is an identity psalm (web_mt_offset_map.json: rule=identity, web_verses=mt_verses=28, mt_title_verses=[], superscription note 'prefix_of_v1'); the web:Ps.35.0 = oshb:Ps.35.1 title pseudo-ref is correctly formed per the owner ruling even though the title is not a separately MT-counted verse. No Hebrew is quoted in this row so no dual-cite obligation applies to the content verses. I independently tested the strongest rival I could construct against this 10-verse span (splitting at web.3|4, imperative-to-Yahweh vs. jussive-imprecation-about-enemies, a mood/addressee shift comparable to drivers used elsewhere in this cluster) but the text itself argues against it: web.3 ('Tell my soul, I am your salvation') and web.9-10 ('My soul shall be joyful... rejoice in his salvation') form a verifiable soul/salvation lexical inclusio bracketing the full span (checked against verse_map_web.json), which is a stronger tier-1 cohesion signal than the internal mood shift is a division signal. High confidence is justified. The rejected_alternative (v9-10 as its own unit) is the correct rival to name and is properly dismissed on same-addressee/same-subject grounds.

The one Hebrew quote, ediei chamas (oshb:Ps.35.11), collates at byte tier; the parenthetical gloss 'literally witnesses of violence' is an accurate literal rendering of edei (construct plural of ed, witness) chamas (violence), correctly held apart from WEB's dynamic 'Unrighteous witnesses' and clearly labeled as a translation note rather than a curly-quoted WEB citation. The new-subject seam at web.11 (unrighteous witnesses, unrelated to the enemies-in-a-net imagery of the prior cycle) and the petition-climax-to-vow close at web.17-18 are both verifiable from the text. This is an identity psalm so no dual-cite is required on the bare web: refs. High confidence is warranted: both the opening and closing seams are clean tier-1 discourse-frame shifts.

No Hebrew quoted; all boundary claims are checkable against WEB text directly. The third petition restart at web.19 and the closing vow at web.28 are accurate. I tested two rival internal seams: the direct-address turn at web.22 ('You have seen it, Yahweh') and the curse-to-blessing turn at web.26|27 ('let them be disappointed... / let those who favor my righteous cause shout for joy'). The row explicitly names and reasons through the first (correctly, since direct address to Yahweh recurs without a fresh grievance, consistent with the escalating-address pattern already established at web:35.17); the second is jussive-to-jussive (no addressee or discourse-frame change) and both verses feed the same web.27-28 vow close the row's own device_notes already treats as one unit, so neither rival out-warrants the row's span. High confidence is reasonable. Tiling across all of Ps 35 (web:35.1-35.28 total) is exact at 28/28 verses with no gaps or overlaps.
